name: Bancha

origin.regionNote: nationwide — a style, not a garden

harvest.window: summer and autumn, or first-flush coarse leaf

pluckStandard: larger, more mature leaf and stems

processing.description: Steamed like sencha, often lighter rolling; some regional banchas are roasted or lactic-fermented and live on their own pages.
Coarser leaf and stems; everyday Japanese green, not a failed sencha.

gongfu.curveException: Japanese greens go long–short–long: the first cool steep needs time, the second is quick because the leaf is open, the third lengthens again.

decoction.when: a kettle on the table, not a timed steep
decoction.notes: 煮茶 — hojicha and bancha are often simmered. The roast already did the work; heat just lifts it.

water.note: Hotter than gyokuro; bancha is the household workhorse.

storage: Airtight pantry is acceptable; less fragile than gyokuro.

shelfLife.window: within a year of roast or packing

summary: Everyday Japanese green from later or coarser leaf: simple, hot, and built for a pot.
